title: Exposed .env file
detail: Environment files commonly contain database credentials, API keys, and secret tokens.
recommendation: Ensure .env is excluded from the web root/build output and blocked at the web-server config.

title: Exposed .git/config
detail: A reachable .git directory usually allows reconstructing the full source tree and commit history, including any secrets ever committed.
recommendation: Remove the .git directory from the deployed web root, or block /.git/ at the reverse proxy.

title: Exposed .git/HEAD
detail: Confirms a reachable .git directory even if config is blocked separately; tools like git-dumper can reconstruct the repo from this alone.
recommendation: Block /.git/ entirely at the reverse proxy, not just individual files.

title: Exposed AWS credentials file
detail: Would expose AWS access keys if present, allowing full account compromise depending on the key's permissions.
recommendation: Never deploy credential files into the web root; use an instance role or a secrets manager instead.

title: Exposed WordPress config backup
detail: Editor/deploy-tool backup files (.bak, .old, ~) of wp-config.php contain the database password and secret keys in plaintext.
recommendation: Remove backup files from the web root; configure the editor/deploy pipeline to avoid leaving them behind.

title: Exposed config backup file
detail: Backup copies of config files often bypass PHP execution and are served as plaintext, leaking any embedded secrets.
recommendation: Remove backup/editor artifact files from the web root before deploying.

title: Exposed backup archive
detail: A world-readable full-site or database backup archive can expose source code, credentials, and user data.
recommendation: Store backups outside the web root, or require authentication to reach them.

title: Exposed .htpasswd file
detail: Contains hashed HTTP Basic Auth credentials that can be cracked offline if the hashing scheme is weak.
recommendation: Block access to dotfiles (.ht*) at the web-server config; this is enabled by default on most servers but worth confirming.

title: Exposed SSH private key
detail: A private key served from the web root would allow SSH access to any host that trusts the matching public key.
recommendation: Audit how the key ended up in the web root and rotate it immediately if this is a real finding.

title: Exposed docker-compose.yml
detail: Compose files frequently contain internal service names, ports, and sometimes plaintext environment secrets.
recommendation: Keep deployment manifests out of the web root.

title: Exposed Apache server-status page
detail: mod_status left open can leak internal IPs, in-flight request URLs (sometimes including session tokens in query strings), and server load.
recommendation: Restrict /server-status to localhost/trusted IPs in the Apache config.

title: Exposed Spring Boot Actuator endpoint
detail: Actuator endpoints (health, env, beans, heapdump) can leak configuration and, in the worst case, application secrets or memory dumps.
recommendation: Restrict actuator endpoints to an internal management port/network, and disable sensitive ones in production.

title: Exposed phpinfo() page
detail: phpinfo() discloses the full PHP configuration, loaded extensions, and server environment variables.
recommendation: Remove phpinfo.php (or equivalent debug scripts) from production deployments.

title: security.txt present
detail: Not a vulnerability — indicates the organization publishes a vulnerability-disclosure/security contact policy.
recommendation: Use the published contact for any findings from this assessment that fall outside the agreed scope.
